stem: A hospitalized adult receiving parenteral nutrition has repeated blood-glucose values above the prescribed goal. Which nursing response best reflects current PN safety guidance?

options.A: Continue the current infusion without reporting the trend because established parenteral nutrition does not require ongoing glucose-control review once the prescription is stable.
options.B: Stop the parenteral nutrition and remove the central venous catheter because repeated hyperglycemia by itself establishes a catheter-related bloodstream infection.
options.C: Increase dextrose delivery so the client becomes accustomed to the carbohydrate load, then reassess glucose after the revised infusion has been running for several hours.
options.D: Continue prescribed monitoring, report the persistent glucose trend, and collaborate with the prescribing or nutrition team to restore glucose control.

rationale: ASPEN's current Parenteral Nutrition Care Pathway directs clinicians to initiate a monitoring protocol and reevaluate PN therapy, and its PN quality-improvement step explicitly includes maintaining glucose control. Repeated glucose values above the prescribed goal therefore warrant continued monitoring, reporting, and coordinated reassessment of the PN and other clinical contributors. A incorrectly dismisses ongoing glucose management. B confuses hyperglycemia with proof of CLABSI; ASPEN lists infection control as a separate PN safety domain. C would increase the carbohydrate load despite an already elevated glucose trend. Therefore D is the uniquely appropriate response.
educational_objective: During parenteral nutrition, use the prescribed monitoring protocol to recognize persistent hyperglycemia, report the trend, and collaborate on measures to restore glucose control while assessing other clinical contributors.
source_organization: American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (ASPEN)
source_version_date: PN Care Pathway listed by ASPEN as April 2025; live pathway current 2026
source_locator: Step 9 Monitor and Reevaluate Patient: initiate monitoring protocol and evaluate efficacy/goals of therapy. Step 11 Parenteral Nutrition Quality Improvement Program: maintain glucose control; implement infection control for CLABSI is listed separately as another quality/safety domain.
source_claim_supported: Parenteral nutrition care requires ongoing monitoring and reevaluation, including maintenance of glucose control; CLABSI prevention is a separate safety domain rather than something diagnosed by hyperglycemia alone.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp. 38–41: administer and monitor parenteral therapies, evaluate client response to treatment, monitor laboratory values, and communicate clinically significant treatment-related changes.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — parenteral nutrition glucose monitoring and response
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four responses to eliminate the uniquely-long keyed answer and make the distractors realistic PN-management errors involving failure to report, misdiagnosis of CLABSI, and inappropriate dextrose escalation.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Parenteral nutrition — persistent hyperglycemia monitoring and safety
audit_findings.stem: PASS — identifies repeated values above a prescribed goal without imposing an unsupported universal numeric threshold.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — established PN still requires ongoing monitoring and reevaluation, including glucose control.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — catheter infection is an important PN complication, but hyperglycemia alone does not establish CLABSI and does not by itself justify line removal.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — increasing dextrose despite persistent hyperglycemia moves away from the stated glucose-control goal.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS — directly reflects monitoring, reevaluation, glucose control, and coordinated management; uniquely best.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — only D responds to the glucose trend without abandoning monitoring or inventing a diagnosis or counterproductive nutrition change.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A ignores monitoring, B conflates hyperglycemia with CLABSI, and C worsens the carbohydrate burden despite elevated glucose.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — the keyed answer is not the longest and the alternatives remain comparable in clinical complexity and specificity.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes parenteral therapy and treatment-response monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether PN should simply be stopped or the line removed; ASPEN specifically frames glucose control as a monitoring/quality domain and CLABSI prevention separately, leaving coordinated reassessment in D uniquely best.
